messages:
marta: seeing steady mem growth on dedicated-rt-4 during long streaming chats that call tools repeatedly. started around 03:10 UTC. nodes hit OOM+restart after ~6h of heavy convo loops. anyone else?

liam: yep noticed traces in staging yesterday. looks like KV pages keep accumulating even after tool loop finishes. not typical eviction pattern.

shawn: eng-bot fired this morning: `alert: high_resident_memory dedicated-rt-4` at 03:14 :warning:

eng-bot: [auto] Node dedicated-rt-4 resident memory 87% -> 96%. snapshot saved to /var/log/rt/mem-snap-1769998800.txt

marta: pasted the pmap delta from before/after a 2h streaming session:```
before: total 42.1G
after: 55.3G
heap: +10.2G
anonymous: +3.0G
mapped: +0.0G
```

liam: can you grab jemalloc stats and the KV cache metrics? specifically evict_count, pages_in_use, frag_ratio.

marta: got them. KV metrics from /metrics/kv-cache:```
kv_pages_in_use: 20480
kv_pages_allocated_total: 31200
kv_evictions_total: 128
kv_eviction_rate: 0.018
kv_page_reuse_hits: 640
kv_page_fragmentation_ratio: 1.27
```

marta: jemalloc stats (summarized):```
active: 52G
allocated: 34G
mapped: 56G
metadata: 1.2G
retain: 12G
```

shawn: interesting. evictions are happening but retain is high -> allocator not returning pages to OS. frag_ratio 1.27 suggests fragmentation but not huge. might be KV pages pinned due to outstanding references (streaming tool loops keep KV shards referenced?).

liam: also saw this in `perf` heap-sample: many live references from the streaming kiosk task. kernel selection commit `opt/kernel-select-v2` landed on 1769950000, maybe changed allocation alignment or page size usage?

marta: timeline matches. kernel-select-v2 + new batching heuristics (batching window increase) landed last week. could change access patterns so KV pages are less reusable.

ada (typo corrected to ada): adding a note: in one repro I could force reuse by manually compacting KV map by calling `kv_cache.compact()` and RSS dropped ~6GB over a minute. so reclaim is possible.

marta: logs from compact run:```
[2026-03-16T03:45:12Z] kv_cache.compact() started
[2026-03-16T03:45:12Z] scanned 31200 pages, merged 8200 fragments
[2026-03-16T03:46:05Z] reclaimed 6.1G resident
[2026-03-16T03:46:07Z] compact complete
```

shawn: that confirms pages aren't fully reachable but GC/compaction isn't running automatically during streaming. two hypotheses: (1) compaction suppressed because of continuous small allocations from streaming tasks, (2) kernel selection/batching changed page-size or slab choices so freed pages are nonstandard and go to retain.

liam: proposal: enable periodic compaction (config flag) for a subset of nodes and run A/B for 24h. also revert kernel-select-v2 on a canary pool to see delta.

marta: I can flip `kv.compaction.enabled=true` on canary-rt-1 and revert kernel-select on canary-rt-2. will run a controlled streaming load (tool-loop-heavy) and capture jemalloc & kv metrics every 10m.

ada: also suggest adding a short-circuit in tool-loop code to release KV references earlier: `with kv_cache.lease(key):` -> make lease drop immediately after tool response. low-risk change.

eng-bot: [task] Created issue INF-2338: "Investigate KV page retention during long streaming tool loops" assigned to @marta, @liam, @shawn. link: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-2338 :white_check_mark:

marta: quick checklist before A/B:
- snapshot current kernel-select-v2 commit hash
- enable kv.compaction.enabled on canary-rt-1
- revert kernel-select on canary-rt-2
- add jemalloc/exporter at 10m cadence
- add `kv_cache.compact()` toggle endpoint (auth gated)

liam: I'll script the metrics collection and a small tool-loop load generator. plan to run 12h -> evaluate.

shawn: if compaction fixes it, we should upstream a low-overhead background compactor + heuristics to trigger after N tool-loop iterations.

marta: noted. for immediate mitigation I patched the streaming worker to drop KV leases earlier (deployed to canary-rt-1). watching memory now. will update in ~1h.

liam: thanks. ping @oncall if we see more OOMs. :thumbsup:
